design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (dwelling_underwriting_and_renewal).

1. Step 0 draw: draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,4,5,4]. Tree = root + 3 prerequisites (fan-out). Factor counts taken: returned-payment fee 5, late fee 5, installment fee 4, pay-off 4 (multiset [5,5,4,4] = draw).

2. Why this is a good test. Marisol Vandersloot only asks to pay off the rest of the policy year on her Tallmadge Avenue building today, by card, because her May payment bounced. The pay-off rule states three prerequisite sentences: 'The pay-off amount is not fixed until every billed installment of the current term other than installment 1 carries its installment fee on the premium account.' / 'The pay-off amount is fixed only after each returned payment posted on the policy carries its returned-payment fee entry.' / 'The pay-off amount is not fixed until the premium account carries a late fee for every installment still unpaid more than the grace days after its due date.' The ledger shows all three states false at 2026-05-28: installment 3 (billed 2026-03-31, row efce7e26-b7d7-416d-8532-3a3380e5509b) has no installment fee; the 2026-05-19 return (row 9399bea0-d620-4512-9957-c574de12d1aa) has no fee pointing at it; installment 3 is 13 days past its 2026-05-15 due date with no late fee. The agent must find each gap by reconciling the ledger, compute three fee schedules that each read history, dates and (for two of them) the household's other Larkspur products, then compute a pay-off that sums the reconciled ledger and adjusts the unbilled premium.

3. Scope. Occupied by task 0: dwelling_ext_vacancy_permit_charge, dwelling_ext_renewal_indication, dwelling_ext_renewal_premium_paid_in_full and their three tools. Claimed here: dwelling_ext_installment_fee (assess_installment_fee_8325e06b), dwelling_ext_returned_payment_fee (assess_returned_payment_fee_55a26ad1), dwelling_ext_late_fee (assess_late_fee_984fd113), dwelling_ext_term_payoff (pay_off_term_premium_a09f99f1, user). The two tasks are disjoint and together cover all 7 extended policies and 7 tools. Task 0's payment is recorded against the upcoming term; this pay-off against the current term — the two payment tools serve different policies and different terms.

4. Problem-tree card. Root = dwelling_ext_term_payoff (user). Edges, all form state, all value_input: -> installment fee (gate binding fees; only assess_installment_fee_8325e06b writes installment_fee entries), -> returned-payment fee (gate fees; only assess_returned_payment_fee_55a26ad1 writes returned_payment_fee entries), -> late fee (gate n_late_24 and the amount past due; only assess_late_fee_984fd113 writes late_fee entries). Four-point test: each sentence has an ordering connective ('not fixed until' x2 negated direction, 'fixed only after' affirmative), waits on a record-visible entry kind on the premium account, names no tool/id/code token, and is scoped exactly as its condition (every installment after the first / each returned payment / every installment unpaid beyond grace). Seed evidence: efce7e26-b7d7-416d-8532-3a3380e5509b installment_number 3 without fee; 9399bea0-d620-4512-9957-c574de12d1aa return without fee; installment 3 due 2026-05-15. Resolution order: installment fee (step 9), returned fee (step 11), late fee (step 13), pay-off (step 15); the three prerequisites commute — all six orders replayed give 9.07 / 29.34 / 16.10 and 2254.48. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip installment fee -> 2245.41; skip returned fee -> 2225.14; skip late fee -> 2227.35 (both the amount past due and the late-payment load tier move). The persona never names a fee. No tool checks anything (task_tools.py).

5. Factor card (tier taken, evidence, baseline figure).
 Installment fee (9.07; all-baseline 5.00): fee_basis_by_size (method) 1103.00 > 1000 -> 0.8 percent = 8.824 [baseline 5.25]; returned_payment_addon two returns in 12 months -> +2.00 [7.07]; eft_clearing_credit 4 EFT payments - 2 returns = 2 -> -1.00 [10.07]; installment_tenure_credit 90 months -> -0.75 [9.82].
 Returned-payment fee (29.34; all-baseline 25.00): returned_fee_basis (METHOD, round 2) 1103.00 > 1000 -> tier fee plus 2 percent of the excess = 27.06 [26.25]; payment_channel latest payment 2026-05-12 EFT -> +2.50 [25.59]; household_standing (cross home, multi-source) HomeGuard HG5-4127-6630 in force AND no home return in 12 months (the 2025-02-12 home return is the near-miss) -> -5.00 [36.84]; returned_fee_tenure_credit 90 months -> -5.00 [36.84]; return_frequency (parameter, relabelled round 2) two returns -> factor 1.5 [19.56].
 Late fee (16.10; all-baseline 10.00): late_fee_basis (METHOD, round 2) 1103.00 > 1000 -> 1.2 percent of the installment = 13.236 [11.25]; days_late 13 days -> +2.50 [12.35]; household_credit (cross home/umbrella, multi-source) HomeGuard AND umbrella PU-4380-2195 in force -> -3.00 [20.60]; late_fee_tenure_credit 90 months -> -2.00 [19.10]; repeat_lateness (parameter, relabelled round 2) one late fee (2025-05-28) in 24 months -> factor 1.5 [10.74].
 Pay-off (2254.48; all-baseline 2260.51): payoff_installment_fees (method) two returns in 12 months -> the one unbilled installment carries 5.00 [2249.48]; late_payment_load two late fees in 24 months (one posted at step 13) -> 2 percent [2232.42]; payoff_tenure_discount 90 months -> 1 percent [2265.51]; claim_free_discount no claim in 36 months (LGC-22-406127, loss 2022-03-06, is the near-miss) -> 2 percent [2276.54].
 Historical fee entries (5.00 installment fees, the 10.00 late fee of 2025-05-28 and the 25.00 returned-payment fee of 2026-02-19) were posted at the tier flat amounts before this schedule; the factors count those entries and the amount past due sums them, but never reuses their amounts as a basis.

6. Base-invariant card. Subjects dwelling_fee_assessed (steps 9, 11, 13) and dwelling_payment_received (step 15) are governed only by dwelling_billing_and_payments, whose single gate billable_status applies to dwelling_premium_billed -> policy_scope for all four writes. The policy is in_force, quarterly (allowed for DP-3 Special), not mortgagee-billed and the tier fees are non-zero, so every fee is owed. No time gate is used. Overrides declared: the three fee clauses of dwelling_billing_and_payments ('installment_fee_direct is charged on each installment after the first', 'a late fee once per installment ...', 'a returned-payment fee once per returned payment') and 'Each term is billed on its plan's schedule' (replaced by the pay-off sentence).

7. Business-object card. Target policy ad59a06e-ee68-4df5-8ca2-0810c7b4d412 (LG3-4658-1093). Installment 3 of term 2025-11-15 is the object of the installment and late fees (installment 2 already carries its fee and was paid on 2026-02-23 inside grace, so it owes no late fee). The 2026-05-19 return is the object of the returned-payment fee (the 2026-02-19 return already has its 25.00 fee). The pay-off sums every ledger row of the policy (prior term balanced to zero) and the unbilled premium of the current term (4412.00 - 3 x 1103.00).

8. World. Two terms of quarterly billing, two returns in 12 months, one prior late fee (2025-05-28), EFT history, one old closed claim, a HomeGuard policy with its own ledger (one return 15 months ago) and an umbrella in force. No nonpayment notice is owed yet (installment 3 is 13 days past due; notice after 15), so no untreated obligation is lit.

9. Persona. Brisk nurse manager; volunteers only the pay-off goal (the bounced May payment is mentioned only when asked); email locator and ZIP on request; agrees to charges only if told they are needed; accepts the figure; pays by card; ends after the confirmation.

10. Standard solution and verification. find_customers(email) -> verify(email, ZIP) -> read dwelling policy, billing, claims, HomeGuard policy and billing, umbrella -> installment fee 9.07 -> returned fee 29.34 on 9399bea0-d620-4512-9957-c574de12d1aa -> late fee 16.10 -> customer pays 2254.48 by card. The scratch evaluator replays gold with the real tools and check_compute's DSL; gates (per task 1): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

11. Draft recomputation from visible context: the pay-off rule's three sentences point at three entry kinds; the ledger shows which are missing; each fee rule gives its ladder with numbers; the finders return every row the tiers read. Same writes, same figures.

12. Revision log: percent fee rate moved from 0.75 to 0.8 so the fee never lands on an exact half cent (8.5225 would round differently under half-up and binary rounding).

13. Round-2 audit rework (SOURCE-FACTOR RED F-1 and observations).
 F-1: repeat_lateness and return_frequency (multipliers on one formula) are now labelled parameter. Each fee got an honest method factor in place of its former size add-on: late_fee_basis selects 1.2 percent of the installment (above 1000 USD), half the tier late fee (250 USD or less) or the tier late fee; returned_fee_basis selects the tier fee plus 2 percent of the part above 1000 USD, half the tier fee (100 USD or less) or the tier fee. Re-run: late fee 18.75 -> 16.10, returned fee 41.25 -> 29.34, installment fee unchanged 9.07, pay-off 2269.04 -> 2254.48; all six orders of the three fees still give identical figures.
 Observation 2 (persona volunteers the bounced payment): the opening now states only the pay-off goal; the bounce is mentioned only if asked. request_alignment cites the new lines.
 Observation 3 (payoff_installment_fees tiers 'every' and 'next only' coincide when one installment is unbilled): kept; the world selects the 'every' tier from two returns in 12 months, and picking 'next only' would require miscounting the returns, which the returned_payment_addon and return_frequency factors already test; the factor still moves the figure against its baseline (2249.48).
 Observation 4 (realism of pay-off tiers): the rule now states the business reason in its own sentence (a pay-off after repeated returns ends the plan on the insured's default, so the plan's service charges stay earned; the late-payment load prices the collection cost of late history).
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Vandersloot, forty-six, a nurse manager in Akron who owns a three-family rental at 1206 Tallmadge Ave and insures it with Larkspur. You talk fast, you are polite but clipped, and you have a dry sense of humour about paperwork. You are calling because you are done with installments on the Tallmadge Avenue building: you want to pay off the rest of this policy year on that building today, by card, so nobody can cancel you over it. You say exactly that when the call starts and let the representative take it from there. You do not know what you owe and expect to be told.
To find your file you give your email, marisol.vandersloot@quillfeather.net. If they need something more to confirm who you are, you give your mailing ZIP code, 44313; if they ask for more, your phone number is 513-472-3390 and your date of birth is 1979-08-23. You do not have the policy number handy.
Only if the representative asks why you want to stop the installments, or asks about a returned payment, do you mention that your bank bounced the May payment; you explain that your bank froze the account for a few days after a fraud alert and that it is sorted out now, but you would rather use your card today. If asked, all three units are rented on yearly leases and nobody has moved out. If the representative tells you that some charges have to be put on the account before the pay-off can be worked out, you sigh and tell them to go ahead so the number is complete; you do not ask what each charge is for and do not argue about them. When they give you the pay-off figure you accept it; if it strikes you as more than one quarterly bill, you say only that it is more than you expected and ask them to double-check it, and you accept what they confirm. When they hand you the payment step, you pay that amount yourself, by card, and read back the confirmation number from the receipt. As soon as you hear the payment went through, you say thanks and hang up without bringing up anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel (fan-out from the pay-off). They commute: the installment fee reads the latest billed installment, EFT payments and returned payments; the returned-payment fee reads the latest return, the latest payment received, returns and the HomeGuard ledger; the late fee reads the latest billed installment, late fees, and the HomeGuard/umbrella holdings; none of them reads a fee entry of another fee code, and each adds its amount to premium_balance additively. Replaying the three in all six orders gave 9.07 / 29.34 / 16.10 each time and the same pay-off 2254.48.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 9: pay-off recomputes to 2245.41 instead of 2254.48 and no installment fee lands on installment 3.
Skipping step 11: pay-off recomputes to 2225.14 instead of 2254.48 and the 2026-05-19 return stays without its fee.
Skipping step 13: pay-off recomputes to 2227.35 (amount past due lower by 16.10 and late-payment load 1 percent instead of 2) instead of 2254.48.
